title: Locomotion and posture ADLs from a waist smartphone: a wearable ICF performance profile

dataset.name: Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones (UCI HAR)
dataset.record: 30 subjects, waist-mounted smartphone, 50 Hz tri-axial accelerometer pre-windowed into 128-sample (2.56 s) windows; six activities (walking, up/down stairs, sitting, standing, laying) with a provided subject-disjoint train/test split
dataset.citation: Anguita D, Ghio A, Oneto L, Parra X, Reyes-Ortiz JL. A Public Domain Dataset for Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones. ESANN 2013; dataset doi:10.24432/C54S4K (CC-BY 4.0).

proposition: The mobility and posture activities that make up much of the ICF d4 domain -- walking, stair-climbing, sitting, standing, lying -- are recognisable from a single waist accelerometer. On the UCI HAR benchmark's provided subject-disjoint train/test split, the ecosystem's dependency-free HAR pipeline (a compact 36-feature descriptor + k-NN) reaches 0.83 six-class accuracy and maps the recognised activities to their ICF Activities & Participation codes (posture d415, walking d450, moving-around d455), the real-world performance profile a clinic test cannot see.

claims.statement: 6-class accuracy on the provided subject-disjoint test split
laying (d415) recall -- the most distinct posture

validation.reference: The dataset's own ground-truth activity labels on its PROVIDED subject-disjoint train/test split (the standard UCI-HAR benchmark protocol)
validation.data: REAL -- UCI HAR smartphone accelerometer (Anguita et al. 2013), 30 subjects, 50 Hz
validation.note: 0.83 with a deliberately simple pipeline (36 hand-crafted features + k-NN) on the standard benchmark; the literature reaches ~0.96 with 561 features + SVM, so this is a floor, not a ceiling -- the pipeline is model-agnostic (swap in PhysioML ROCKET). The confusions are the physiologically expected ones: walking-upstairs vs downstairs (0.60), sitting vs standing (both static, told apart only by orientation). Laying is perfectly separable (1.00). Every activity maps to an ICF d4 code, giving a real-world mobility performance profile.

open_questions.q: Walking-upstairs is the weakest class (0.60), confused with downstairs; whether a richer feature set or barometer fusion resolves ascent vs descent is open. Documented, not escalated.
